note: Real slices of real nflverse release assets, byte-for-byte as published, narrowed to Buffalo's weeks 1-3 of the 2024 regular season so the whole corpus stays a few tens of kilobytes. One team over three weeks is deliberate: it carries a full offensive-snap denominator (a lineman at 100% of snaps), a quarterback, backs and receivers with real target shares, players who appear in one file and not the other, and enough weeks for a rolling window and a backtest replay to have something to walk. Every column the upstream release publishes is kept, including the ones no mapper reads yet, so a schema change upstream is visible here as a diff rather than as a silent drop.

entries.filtered: every person the other two slices reference by pfr_id or gsis_id, plus five players who retired after 2023 (Latavius Murray, Matt Breida, DeVante Parker, Jerick McKinnon, Logan Thomas) and the retired centre who shares Josh Allen's name. The retirees are the point: Phase 1 measured them as the reason a roster-snapshot join loses ten points of resolution per season going back, and the two Josh Allens are the case a name join cannot settle and an id join never has to. One pfr_id in the snap-counts slice (AndeAl01) is genuinely absent from the release, which keeps a real unresolved case in the corpus.

season=2024, week=1, team=BUF. Week one only, because week one is the only weekly roster whose knowable-before-the-opener claim is true (the league's cutdown to fifty-three is a deadline in late August) and the only one `preseason_rosters` stores. The slice keeps every status the release emits for one club, so the coarsening in `rosterStatusOf` has an active list, a reserve list, a practice squad and a cut list to be tested against rather than only the happy path.

season=2020, position in QB/RB/WR/TE. One whole skill-position draft class (78 picks, rounds 1-7) rather than a handful of hand-picked rows, because the curve fit reads pick-to-pick spacing and a thin hand-written table would test our understanding of the shape rather than the shape itself. Keeps two real Cole McDonald rows (round 7, pick 224, blank gsis_id) exactly as the release publishes them — a round-seven quarterback pfr never assigned an NFL id — which is the real case `mapDraftPicks` drops rather than a synthetic one.
